body.heading: Two ways to describe
paragraphs: When we describe what something looks like, we use two kinds of words: color words (what color is it?) and shape words (what shape is it?). Together they can describe almost anything you can see.
Let's practice with the world around us.

body.heading: Colors
paragraphs: Red like a strawberry. Blue like the sky. Yellow like the sun. Green like the grass.
Orange like a pumpkin. Purple like a plum. Pink like a flower. Brown like a tree trunk.
Black like the night. White like snow. Gold like treasure. Silver like the moon.

body.heading: Shapes
paragraphs: A circle is round all the way around — like a ball or the sun.
A square has four sides, all the same — like a window.
A triangle has three sides — like a roof or a slice of pie.
A rectangle is a longer square — like a door or a book.
A star has points that twinkle — like the stars in the night sky.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Describe something in the room using one color word and one shape word: 'a round, red clock!' Can others guess it?
2. Go on a shape hunt: find a circle, a square and a triangle without leaving the room.

takeaway: Color words and shape words work as a team to describe anything you can see — a round red ball, a square blue window.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
